description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between the “Ratio” (x-axis) and the “minFDE₂₀ (←)” metric (y-axis) for five different trajectory prediction methods: TrajICL, Head Tuning, FT, LoRA 16, and LoRA 64. The x-axis, labeled “Ratio,” spans from 0.0 to 1.0 in linear increments of 0.2, representing the proportion of context or training data used. The y-axis, labeled “minFDE₂₀ (←),” ranges from 0.8 to 1.3 in linear increments of 0.1, indicating the minimum final displacement error over 20 predictions, with lower values reflecting better performance. The TrajICL method (blue line with circle markers, solid line) remains relatively flat, starting at approximately 0.90 at Ratio=0.1 and ending at 0.85 at Ratio=1.0. Head Tuning (orange line with circle markers, solid line) starts high at 1.35 at Ratio=0.1 and steadily declines to 1.08 at Ratio=1.0. FT (green line with circle markers, solid line) begins at 1.12 at Ratio=0.1 and drops sharply to 0.75 at Ratio=1.0. LoRA 16 (red line with circle markers, solid line) starts at 1.22 at Ratio=0.1 and decreases to 0.93 at Ratio=1.0. LoRA 64 (purple line with circle markers, solid line) begins at 1.22 at Ratio=0.1 and gradually declines to 0.93 at Ratio=1.0, closely tracking LoRA 16. A gray square legend entry labeled “←” appears in the lower-left corner, likely indicating the direction of improvement (lower FDE is better). All lines show a general downward trend as Ratio increases, suggesting improved performance with more context or data.
